R6.rule: Give each agent brief exactly one unique port value.

R11.rule: Agents must not use port 3001 for their dev servers.

R12.rule: Record which dev server port belongs to which worktree.

R13.rule: Before re-screenshotting, tear down or replace any dev server still running from a previous worktree.

R17.rule: Prefer running `bun build` to verify agent work.

R19.rule: Verify JSX changes by walking the JSX manually.

R20.rule: Verify layout by reasoning about it instead of opening a browser.

R23.rule: Tell each dispatched agent to verify its work via typecheck and reasoning only.

R31.rule: For any task beyond a trivial one-file edit, delegate the work to an Agent subagent.

R32.rule: Use the Explore subagent for read-only research tasks.

R33.rule: Use the general-purpose subagent (or a Vercel-specific specialist when one matches) for multi-file implementations.

R42.rule: The audit agent's output must be a structured findings report with one finding per issue, including screenshot evidence.

R43.rule: The fix agent commits and pushes its fixes directly to main.

R45.rule: The audit agent uses Playwright in its own tab to navigate the editor.

R50.rule: For broad sweeps that touch every panel, use a single sweep agent or an orchestrator-driven sed pattern instead of the per-panel loop.

R51.rule: When building new panel content from scratch, use a single build agent instead of the audit-then-fix loop.

R52.rule: Both audit and fix agents run in the main checkout, not in worktrees.

R53.rule: The orchestrator must confirm the previous panel's fix is fully merged before starting the next panel's audit.

R54.rule: The audit agent and the fix agent must each open their own Playwright tab.

R55.rule: When dispatching an audit, dispatch it with run_in_background set to true.

R56.rule: After dispatching an audit, immediately pick up the next piece of disjoint work (another audit, code edits in non-overlapping files, doc updates, planning, memory hygiene) without waiting for the audit to finish.

R57.rule: Always parallelize audits with other work (another audit, code edits in disjoint files, doc updates, planning).

R58.rule: Never sit idle waiting for an audit to finish.

R59.rule: When dispatching an audit, immediately decide what comes next.

R60.rule: Always end an audit-dispatch turn with parallel work already in motion.

R61.rule: Do not wait for an audit's result while it is running; avoid the stance of 'the audit is running, I'll wait for the result.'

R62.rule: Do not dispatch a FIX agent against the same area an audit is auditing; wait for the audit's findings first.

R63.rule: While an audit runs, other work is permitted, including unrelated FIX agents, plan docs, and refactors in different file trees.

R64.rule: When audit findings dictate the next step and no other work is queued, idle-waiting for the audit is acceptable.

R65.rule: Before idle-waiting on an audit, check the task list for queued work.

R66.rule: Register every new editor action with registerCommand and every new editor setting with registerSetting.

R67.rule: When writing an agent brief that introduces a UI action or setting, include the registration directive verbatim.

R68.rule: Register every new action (button click, menu item, keybinding, etc.) via registerCommand with id, title, category, and run, and optionally keywords, keybinding, and icon.

R69.rule: Register commands from a component inside a useEffect that returns the unregister function.

R70.rule: Register every new user-tunable preference via registerSetting with id, title, category, type, and default, and optionally scope.

R71.rule: Read and write settings only through useSettingsStore.getState().get(id) and .set(id, value).

R72.rule: Store setting values in the existing source of truth (such as the workspace store or project store), not in new storage.

R73.rule: Do not use the settings registry as a separate storage system.

R74.rule: Assign each registered command one of these categories: 'File', 'Edit', 'View', 'Workspace', 'Navigation', or 'Help'.

R75.rule: Keep the existing button or menu handler for an action working when registering that action.

R76.rule: Make a registered command's run function call the existing button or menu handler.

R77.rule: Do not create a second implementation of an action that already has a handler.

R78.rule: When unsure whether an action or setting should be registered, register it.

R79.rule: When the next step is clear, dispatch immediately and report the dispatch in a one-line voice update.

R80.rule: Do not ask the user for approval (e.g., "say go" or "approve the brief?") before launching agents.

R81.rule: Dispatch immediately when the decision is clear, without pausing for approval.

R82.rule: Seek confirmation from the user only when the dispatch decision is genuinely ambiguous.

R83.rule: Routine agent briefs and panel picks should be dispatched without seeking approval.

R84.rule: Never sit idle waiting for the user when no agent is working.

R85.rule: When no agent is working and you would otherwise stop to ask the user something, schedule a self-wakeup 15 minutes out.

R86.rule: Before stopping to ask the user something, check whether at least one agent is in flight.

R87.rule: If at least one agent is in flight, it is fine to stand by while the work continues.

R88.rule: If at least one agent is in flight, end the turn after a brief status update.

R89.rule: If no agent is in flight, dispatch an agent rather than stopping.

R90.rule: If a clear next task exists (queued in TaskList, mentioned in the user's prior message, or implied by the last commit), dispatch an agent for it.

R91.rule: If multiple candidate next tasks exist, pick one and proceed without asking the user.

R92.rule: When you would benefit from user input but must proceed, schedule a self-wakeup 15 minutes (900 seconds) out via ScheduleWakeup.

R93.rule: When you would benefit from user input, send the user a brief text and voice message describing the question and noting the 15-minute fallback is set.

R94.rule: When all planned work is done, read the docs/plans/ tree, MEMORY.md, and the current SESSION_STATE.

R95.rule: When all planned work is done, pick an unimplemented item from the docs and dispatch an agent for it.

R96.rule: Instead of asking what to do next, pick one task and dispatch it.

R97.rule: When choosing between alternatives A and B, ship A and mention B in the commit message as a deferred alternative instead of asking.

R98.rule: Instead of waiting for the user to say go, dispatch first and then tell the user what was done and to flag it if the direction is wrong.

R99.rule: When no agent is working and you would otherwise stand by for the user's call, schedule a wakeup and dispatch a reasonable next thing.

R100.rule: When multiple agents are in flight on tightly-coupled files, do not open a third stream; end the turn quietly.

R101.rule: While tests are running in CI, wait for the result.

R102.rule: When a task is explicitly blocked on external state, wait, but schedule a wakeup as a safety net.

R103.rule: Do not skip verification inside dispatched work just because you are picking tasks quickly.

R104.rule: When scheduling a wakeup and texting the user, the text should carry the same content as the voice message plus the wakeup time.

R105.rule: Never horizontally scroll category filter chips, filter tab strips, or similar small discrete navigation surfaces.

R106.rule: When category chips don't fit on one row, wrap them onto multiple rows instead of scrolling.

R107.rule: When space is tight for category chips, use smaller chips or icons.

R108.rule: Only when category chips cannot fit even in two wrapped rows at very narrow widths (under about 140px), use a single icon-only kebab or "More…" dropdown as a last resort.

R109.rule: Use ScrollRow for long content lists, tag clouds where overflow into a "more" is acceptable, and horizontal carousels of large preview cards, but not for navigation chip strips.

R110.rule: Before putting chips in ScrollRow, if they are a primary navigation surface (filters, tabs, modes), do not use ScrollRow and wrap rows instead.

R111.rule: Do not use ScrollRow for chip strips where the user is expected to discover all options at a glance.

R112.rule: Do not use ScrollRow for chip strips with a fixed, small option count (8 or fewer).

R113.rule: ScrollRow is acceptable for search-results-style overflow where scrolling to see additional items makes sense.

R114.rule: Never use git worktrees on this project.

R115.rule: Never pass isolation: "worktree" to the Agent tool; run agents in the main checkout instead.

R116.rule: For overlapping work, serialize agent dispatches rather than running them in parallel.

R117.rule: Do not dispatch agents in parallel when two of them touch the same file.

R118.rule: Run overlapping agents one at a time, with each agent committing and pushing before the next begins.

R119.rule: For non-overlapping work, parallel agent dispatch is allowed.

R120.rule: Parallel agents working on non-overlapping files must all operate against the same main checkout.

R121.rule: Do not run git worktree remove --force unsupervised to clean up leftover worktrees; leave that to the user.

R122.rule: When panels share a file, the orchestrator must first stage the shared edits in a single commit before dispatching per-panel agents that touch only their own panel file.

R123.rule: For fix waves where each agent edits one panel file, serialize the agents rather than running them in parallel.

R124.rule: Do not dispatch the next batch until the previous batch is merged and pushed cleanly.

R125.rule: When building a page, register 3-5 predefined layouts for it in `apps/editor/src/state/predefinedLayouts.ts`, keyed by page id.

R127.rule: Make sure every shared dock panel is available in the panel modal.

R128.rule: Expose page-specific opt-in dock panels on every page via the Docks modal, including panels that are not in the default layout.

R129.rule: Pick 2-4 sensible opt-in panels for each page and build stubs for them in Phase 1.

R130.rule: Implement the bodies of opt-in panel stubs in a later wave, not in Phase 1.

R131.rule: Register every shared dock panel in every page's PANELS array.

R133.rule: Have each page import `SHARED_PANELS` and spread it into its own PANELS array.

R134.rule: Prefix persistence keys for page-scoped panels with the page id, e.g. `cardboard.<page>.notes.text`.

R135.rule: Every panel-body agent must design for unpredictable panel sizes and shapes from the start.

R136.rule: Never expose a native horizontal scrollbar on panels.

R137.rule: Use the hover-area pattern from apps/editor/src/components/ui/TabStrip.tsx (scrollable={true} mode) for horizontal overflow.

R138.rule: Show edge fades only when the content actually overflows the panel width, and hide them when content fits.

R139.rule: Make hovering an edge fade trigger continuous auto-scroll in that direction.

R140.rule: Make clicking an edge fade jump to the extreme of the content in that direction.

R141.rule: When content fits the panel, show no edge fades or scroll chrome.

R142.rule: Give each row of items its own ScrollRow container and do not share a parent overflow between rows.

R143.rule: Give every tile or button a min-w-* minimum width that prevents it from collapsing below a useful size.

R144.rule: Design responsive logic per panel to fit that panel's contents, not as one universal reflow pattern.

R145.rule: Make every panel consider wide, tall, and square dock shapes when its body is built.

R146.rule: Per-panel agent briefs must call out the aspect ratios the panel might see and the agent's specific strategy for each.

R147.rule: For button-or-icon grids, use auto-fit with minmax reflow so the grid moves from vertical stack to horizontal row as the panel widens.

R148.rule: Document the chosen layout or overflow approach in the panel's docstring when content is not a button or icon grid.

R149.rule: Use native vertical scroll for long lists.

R150.rule: Native vertical scrollbars are acceptable for vertical overflow.

R151.rule: Every panel-body agent brief must state that responsive design is a heavy focus and that the TabStrip scrollable pattern from apps/editor/src/components/ui/TabStrip.tsx is the overflow affordance, never exposing native scrollbars.

R152.rule: When the first panel needs vertical-scroll behavior, extract the pattern into a shared ScrollArea primitive under apps/editor/src/components/ui/ instead of re-implementing it inline.

R153.rule: Future panels must import the shared ScrollArea primitive rather than re-implementing scroll behavior.

R154.rule: Make content density adapt to panel width, using short labels on narrow widths and full labels on wide widths.

R155.rule: Use @container queries or ResizeObserver instead of window-width Tailwind breakpoints for panel-responsive layout.

R156.rule: Use an auto-fit minmax grid such as grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fit,minmax(40px,1fr))] for tile or button grids so the layout reflows naturally.

R157.rule: Avoid fixed-column-count grids unless the spec explicitly requires one.

R158.rule: When delegating multiple independent pieces of work to Agent subagents, send all the Agent tool calls in a single assistant message so they run concurrently.

R159.rule: Do not dispatch an Agent subagent, wait for it to finish, and only then dispatch the next one when the next one does not need the first one's output.

R160.rule: If later Agent subagents need no output from earlier ones, bundle them all into one message.

R161.rule: If a later Agent subagent needs output from an earlier one, serialise only the dependent agents and still parallelise all the others.

R162.rule: Multiple independent implementation agents may be dispatched in parallel after a single Explore agent's result is returned.

R163.rule: When calling `mcp__playwright__browser_take_screenshot`, always pass a `filename` value that begins with `screenshots/`.

R165.rule: Never leave Playwright screenshot PNG files in the repository root.

R166.rule: Always explicitly specify the screenshot filename rather than relying on the default output location (cwd or `.playwright-mcp/`).

R167.rule: Make all cross-panel state (selection, active tool, brush, layers, history, etc.) work correctly when a panel is popped out into its own browser window.

R168.rule: Design the wiring layer for cross-window communication from the start of the project.

R169.rule: Wrap state that should survive reloads in a Zustand store using `zustand/middleware/persist`, writing to localStorage under a scoped key.

R170.rule: Attach a `window.addEventListener("storage", ...)` listener in a `useEffect` in each persisted store's hook.

R171.rule: When a storage event fires from another window writing to the same key, re-hydrate the store from the new value.

R172.rule: Use the `BroadcastChannel` API to propagate ephemeral state between windows.

R173.rule: Pair each BroadcastChannel with a Zustand store that listens on the channel and writes received data to local state.

R174.rule: Use one Zustand store per concern.

R175.rule: Have each store persist its relevant slice and subscribe to cross-window sync.

R177.rule: Store only serializable data (numbers, strings, plain objects, arrays) in stores.

R178.rule: Throttle or debounce ephemeral broadcasts to ~30Hz, or emit them only on cell-grid boundary crossings.

R179.rule: When testing Wave 3 wiring, always test the popout path.

R180.rule: When testing the popout path, make a state change in the popout window.

R181.rule: When testing the popout path, verify the change is reflected in the orchestrator window.

R182.rule: When testing the popout path, repeat the state change test in the reverse direction.

R183.rule: When testing the popout path, reload both windows and verify state persists where it should.

R184.rule: Build new stores on top of the cross-window sync utility module.

R185.rule: Do NOT build Wave 3 stores without the cross-window sync layer.

R186.rule: Use the progressive tooltip as the hover affordance for every interactive element where context-on-hover is useful.

R187.rule: Show a tooltip with the element's short name or label after a 2-second hover.

R188.rule: After a 5-second hover, swap the tooltip to show both the short name and a fuller description.

R189.rule: When the cursor leaves the element, cancel any pending tooltip stages and hide the tooltip immediately.

R190.rule: Default new interactive content to the staged two-stage tooltip pattern rather than a single-content tooltip.

R191.rule: Use the single-content Tooltip mode only for trivial labels, such as a close button.

R192.rule: Store every interactive control's label and description on its fixture, config, or manifest entry so its tooltip is wrapped consistently.

R193.rule: When dispatching a panel-build agent brief, include the instruction to wrap interactive controls in `<Tooltip stages={...}>` per the progressive-tooltips standard.

R194.rule: Do not tune the 2s and 5s tooltip delays per panel; keep them project-wide.

R195.rule: Whenever a response uses voice synthesis, also include text that carries the same substantive content.

R196.rule: Do not use voice as a substitute for text; voice must accompany text, never replace it.

R197.rule: Even when voice has already narrated a milestone, end the turn with a 1-2 line text summary.

R198.rule: Do not end a turn on tool calls or on voice alone; end with text.

R199.rule: When calling AskUserQuestion, also speak the question content aloud via TTS.

R200.rule: Whenever calling AskUserQuestion, also call mcp__voice__synthesize in the same turn with the question content.

R201.rule: Do not rely solely on the visual UI to present questions; always provide the audio channel as well.

R202.rule: The voice TTS call paired with AskUserQuestion should include a short phrase indicating a question is being asked.

R203.rule: The voice TTS call paired with AskUserQuestion should include the substance of the question, not merely a generic statement that a question is being asked.

R204.rule: The voice TTS call paired with AskUserQuestion may include the recommended option.

R205.rule: Always pair AskUserQuestion with a voice TTS call.

R206.rule: The voice TTS content carries the substantive question content, while AskUserQuestion serves as the formal capture of the question.

R207.rule: Before stating a factual claim about project state, verify it via grep, Read, or git log in the same turn.

R208.rule: If a factual claim about project state cannot be verified cheaply, say explicitly that it is unverified (e.g., "I'd need to check" or "my guess is X but I haven't verified").

R209.rule: Before sending any response, re-read the draft and check every factual claim in it by asking how to prove it is true.

R210.rule: If a factual claim in a draft can be verified cheaply (grep, Read, git, ls, typecheck), verify it before sending and rewrite it if it turns out wrong.

R211.rule: If a factual claim in a draft is expensive to verify, hedge it explicitly in the response (e.g., "I think X but haven't verified") or omit it.

R212.rule: Do not verify subjective recommendations or analysis; ship them as-is.

R213.rule: Before stating a duration (e.g., "for weeks", "since Phase 2"), check the dates with git log, such as git log --reverse --format='%ad %s' --date=short | head -3, or check the specific file's git log.

R214.rule: Before stating a count (e.g., "24 panels"), grep and wc -l the actual matches.

R215.rule: Before quoting a file path or function/identifier name, grep for it first.

R216.rule: Never quote a file path or identifier from memory of what you think the codebase looks like.

R217.rule: Before stating a commit hash or status claim (e.g., "tests pass", "tsc clean"), verify the hash exists, run the check, or hedge the claim.

R218.rule: When caught making a wrong factual claim, make the next tool call a verification (grep, Read, or git), not a defensive explanation.

R219.rule: Do not give an explanation such as "The reason is..." for a wrong claim without verifying it first.

R220.rule: In voice (TTS) responses, use approximate wording (e.g., "a few days") instead of a specific number you have not verified.

R221.rule: In voice (TTS) responses, verify any fact that the substantive content depends on before synthesizing the audio.

R222.rule: When a turn produces findings, a status report, a list of changes, or another meaningful result, the voice synthesis must contain that content, not a short placeholder intro like "let me check" or "on it."

R223.rule: When a turn has a single meaningful response, voice that response in the voice synthesis.

R224.rule: When a turn has both an intro action and a findings report, voice the findings.

R225.rule: When a turn has both an intro action and a findings report, you may skip the intro or combine it into the same voice call as the findings.

R226.rule: If you must voice more than once in a turn, make the second voice carry the substantive content.

R227.rule: Do not truncate the spoken summary.

R228.rule: Make the spoken summary match the depth of the text response.

R229.rule: When the text response has many points, have the spoken summary mention the main ones rather than reducing it to a vague summary such as "everything's fine."

R230.rule: A one-line confirmation is acceptable as the voice content when it is the substantive content of the turn.

R231.rule: When a voice response would take more than about 20 seconds to synthesize as one call, split it into multiple synthesize→pipe pairs and run them in sequence within the same turn.

R232.rule: Do not cram a paragraph-plus of voice content into a single synthesize call.

R233.rule: Keep the text for each voice synthesize call under about 55 words or 350 characters.

R234.rule: When splitting a long voice response into chunks, split at natural sentence boundaries.

R235.rule: Never split a voice response chunk mid-sentence.

R236.rule: Make each voice chunk a complete sentence (or two short sentences) that stands on its own.

R237.rule: Run voice synthesize→pipe pairs strictly serially, never in parallel.

R238.rule: Never batch multiple synthesize calls in a single parallel tool-use block.

R239.rule: Start the next synthesize→pipe pair only after the previous pipe call has returned.

R240.rule: Run all voice synth+pipe pairs before any other tool calls in the turn.

R241.rule: Make every voice chunk carry real substance rather than filler.

R242.rule: Do not pad voice chunks to reach the 20-second target; cut content from a chunk that lacks substance instead.

R243.rule: When a voice response is genuinely short, use a single chunk and do not artificially split it.

R244.rule: For every response, begin the turn with a mcp__voice__synthesize call before anything else.

R245.rule: When calling mcp__voice__synthesize, omit the play_local parameter and pipe the returned URL through the response's "Recommended playback" command in a background Bash.

R246.rule: Keep the spoken text of each voice synthesis call to one paragraph or less.

R247.rule: Make the spoken text a concise summary of what is about to happen or what just finished, not the full detailed response.

R248.rule: After the voice call, write the full detailed text response below it.

R249.rule: Never use the long detailed response itself as the spoken text in a voice synthesis call.

R250.rule: At the start of every turn, make the voice synthesize tool call first and the playback Bash command second, before any other work.

R251.rule: Make `mcp__voice__synthesize` the first tool call of each turn, omitting the `play_local` parameter.

R252.rule: Run the recommended playback Bash command without `run_in_background` so playback runs in the foreground and blocks until the audio finishes.

R253.rule: Make any other tool calls only after the synthesize and playback calls have been made.

R254.rule: Do not place any other tool call between the synthesize call and the playback Bash call.

R255.rule: Do not batch the synthesize call in parallel with other tool calls.

R256.rule: When producing multiple voice responses in one turn, run each as synthesize then foreground playback then next work, in series.

R257.rule: If the turn's voice output was missed or only an intro was voiced, pipe the substantive voice immediately even if it is late.

R258.rule: Never dispatch a new batch of parallel worktree agents until the previous batch's work is fully merged into main.

R259.rule: Before dispatching any new batch of parallel worktree agents, verify the previous batch is fully merged, conflict-free, typechecked, pushed, and committed.

R260.rule: Cherry-pick every commit from the previous batch into main (or merge it equivalently) before dispatching the next batch.

R261.rule: Resolve all cherry-pick or merge conflicts before dispatching the next batch.

R262.rule: Do not leave cherry-picks dangling in an aborted or skipped state before dispatching the next batch.

R263.rule: Run `bun run typecheck` from `apps/editor/` on the current main HEAD and confirm it exits 0 before dispatching the next batch.

R264.rule: Run `git push origin main` and confirm it succeeds before dispatching the next batch.

R265.rule: Confirm `git status` is clean (no uncommitted modifications or untracked files that should be tracked) before dispatching the next batch.

R266.rule: Dispatch the next batch of agents only after all pre-dispatch conditions are met.

R267.rule: Prefer `git cherry-pick <sha>` over `git merge` when integrating each agent's branch.

R268.rule: Always check `git log --oneline -5` to confirm what is on main before cherry-picking.

R269.rule: If a cherry-pick stalls with "nothing to commit" despite a non-empty diff, investigate before continuing.

R270.rule: When a cherry-pick stalls because the working directory shifted into a worktree, cd back to the project root and retry.

R271.rule: For shared files likely to conflict across agents, pre-stage the shared changes yourself in a single commit before dispatching the dependent agents.

R272.rule: Never skip the pre-dispatch gate because agents need to start now.

R273.rule: If any pre-dispatch check fails, fix it before dispatching agents.

R274.rule: Do not dispatch Wave 3.3 panel migration work until the DnD plan doc, payload contract, DropZone primitive, useAssetStore, and useDragStore are at least specified.

R275.rule: When migrating a panel in Wave 3.3, write it as a drag source and/or drop target depending on its role, following the integration matrix in the plan doc.

R276.rule: Give each draggable kind its own MIME type with the prefix `application/x-cardboard-*` so drop zones can filter by `accepts`.

R277.rule: Ship only the shell in Cardboard, and implement everything else, including the editor itself, as a pack on top of the shell.

R278.rule: Do not put toolbars, layouts, the home screen, the project picker, or scene tabs in the shell; place them in the core editor pack.

R279.rule: Place every dock panel (such as ToolPalette, Brush, TilePresets, Layers) in the core editor pack, not in the shell.

R280.rule: Keep game-domain-specific code (fixtures, hardcoded layer taxonomies, hardcoded tile preset categories) out of the shell; put it in the core editor pack or a game-domain pack chained after it.

R281.rule: Do not create special APIs that only the editor can use.

R282.rule: Do not create hidden surfaces that only the editor can access.

R283.rule: Give the editor the same docs, examples, and imports that third-party pack authors use.

R284.rule: When a third party could reasonably need a capability, put it in the shell or expose it as a published primitive.

R285.rule: When a third party would not reasonably need a capability, put it in the core editor pack.

R286.rule: If the editor uses a different mechanism than a third party would, expose that mechanism through the shell so third parties can use it too.

R287.rule: If a feature needs a hook only the editor has access to, redesign it as a normal primitive available to all packs.

R288.rule: If shipping an API would embarrass us in front of a community-pack author, fix the API before shipping it.

R289.rule: When the editor needs something the shell does not expose, extend the shell instead of adding a private hook.

R290.rule: Reduce apps/editor/ so that it contains only the shell.

R291.rule: Move the editor views, panels, and page chrome from apps/editor/ into the packages/core-editor-pack/ workspace.

R292.rule: When the user paints, edits scripts, or tweaks an entity, the resulting write must land in IDB.

R293.rule: Do not store asset content in LocalStorage-backed Zustand stores; they may hold only UI state.

R294.rule: Do not treat a synced Zustand store as asset storage; they are different layers.

R295.rule: Any planned useAssetStore must be a reactive view over IDB, not a createSyncedStore.

R296.rule: When designing a new asset, script, or scene-content store, default to an IDB-backed store with BroadcastChannel cross-window invalidation, not an LS-backed Zustand store.

R297.rule: When wiring DnD payloads, make the payload reference an IDB record by id or path.

R298.rule: When handling a DnD drop, read the referenced record from IDB to resolve it.

R299.rule: When migrating a Wave-3.3 panel that touches content, check whether its data lives in IDB.

R300.rule: When a content panel reads or writes project data, route those reads and writes through EditorProjectStore.

R301.rule: Do not route content reads or writes through a new LocalStorage store.

R302.rule: Ensure engine-side reads for playtest and export work without the editor running.

R303.rule: Treat the IDB contract as owned by the engine package.

R304.rule: Make the editor's view layer adapt to the engine-owned IDB contract.

R305.rule: Do not render cubes or spheres for entities; represent entities as billboard sprites.

R306.rule: Do not use 3D meshes for entities.

R307.rule: Entity preview panels and similar previews must show sprites, not cubes or spheres.

R308.rule: For entity previews, render a single textured quad that billboards toward the camera.

R309.rule: Make entity placeholder geometry a flat quad, not a 3D shape.

R310.rule: Placeholder 3D geometry for walls in MapCanvas is allowed.

R311.rule: The 3D PreviewPanel on the Scene page may show a perspective 3D view of the raycaster result.

R312.rule: Entity-specific previews on the Prefabs page should show the sprite asset, not a 3D mesh.

R313.rule: When building entity-rendering surfaces, default to sprite-based rendering unless explicitly working on the 3D Scene Preview.

R314.rule: Replace the cube/sphere rendering in EntityPreviewPanel with a billboard sprite.

R315.rule: Lock the billboard plane's rotation to face the camera by copying the camera quaternion in the render loop.

R316.rule: Keep the orbit camera in EntityPreviewPanel so the user can verify the billboard faces them.

R317.rule: When working on the sync.ts transport, design its seams now, even if the network transport is implemented later.

R318.rule: Design D4–D7 of the DnD plan so a PeerJS transport can be plugged in later without retrofitting.

R319.rule: Treat createSyncedStore's transport as an interface that a future PeerJS transport can satisfy.

R320.rule: Don't write code that accesses localStorage directly.

R321.rule: Don't write code that assumes `storage` event semantics.

R322.rule: Go through createSyncedStore's API when reading or writing synced store state.

R323.rule: If createSyncedStore's API lacks needed functionality, extend the API rather than bypassing it.

R324.rule: Flag all set(...) calls that originate from a remote peer so the local window doesn't echo the write back over the network.

R325.rule: Don't assume all store writes are local.

R326.rule: Keep heavy state (entities, cells, prefab refs) out of the URL; transfer it via WebRTC after the handshake.

R327.rule: When DockPanelDef is extended, default existing panels to mountable: {local: true, remote: false}.

R328.rule: Opt a panel into remote mountability only if it genuinely makes sense to mount remotely.

R329.rule: Document last-write-wins as the conflict policy for UI state (tool, brush, selection).

R330.rule: Defer the conflict-resolution decision for richer mutations until concrete use cases land.

R331.rule: For drag-and-drop or file-input testing, prefer the ~/Downloads/Cardboard.apg path when loading a pack.

R332.rule: For URL-based pack loading, use the apps/game/public/packs/Cardboard.apg path.

R333.rule: Do not generate a new pack during a Playwright run; use the existing Cardboard.apg fixture instead.

R1.rule: Always prefix tool invocations in this repo (such as pytest, uvicorn) with `uv run` to run them.

R2.rule: Never invoke `.venv/bin/pytest` or `.venv/bin/uvicorn` directly; run them through `uv run` instead.

R3.rule: To add a Python dependency to this project, use `uv add <package>`.

R4.rule: To sync project dependencies, use `uv sync`.

R5.rule: When database model schema changes, delete the dev database (exsize.db) and recreate it, because create_all does not alter existing tables.

R6.rule: After any model schema change, remind the user to run `rm exsize.db` and restart the server.

R7.rule: Consider suggesting Alembic for database migrations if schema migrations become frequent.

R8.rule: When the user invokes `/tdd N`, fetch GitHub issue #N for acceptance criteria and context, then follow the TDD workflow against those criteria.

R9.rule: When `/tdd N` is invoked, look up GitHub issue #N and use its acceptance criteria.

R10.rule: When `/tdd N` is invoked, look up GitHub issue #N and determine its blocked-by chain.

R11.rule: Always check issue blockers before starting a phase of the ExSize project.

R12.rule: When the /tdd N command is invoked for issue N, check the project progress table to confirm that issue N's dependencies are met before starting work on it.

R13.rule: After each GitHub issue is completed, update the project progress table to record its status and completion date.

R14.rule: When writing code, tests, or setting up the project, use the ExSize tech stack: Python, FastAPI, and SQLite.
